notes: Self pollen combined with or preceding cross pollen markedly reduced fruit production; authors link marked protandry at least partly to avoidance of this interference.

study_design: 138-flower controlled timing experiment with 1380 hand pollinations
notes: Prior or simultaneous self pollen strongly reduces fruit/seed set after cross pollen; cited source does not establish a separate temporal/spatial architecture that resolves the conflict.

study_design: stigma-closure manipulation with pollen export and selfing measurements
notes: Direct experiment: stigma closure increases anther-stigma separation and more than doubles pollen export while minimally changing intrafloral selfing; strong male-female interference case.

study_design: controlled self-pollen precedence and outcross-pollen performance experiment
notes: Self pollen reduces compatible-pollen germination and sometimes seed set. The source explicitly reports both spatial and temporal segregation of pollen and stigma presentation, so the joint nonstructural architecture is retained rather than forced into one mode.

shared_structure: repeated simultaneously hermaphroditic flowers within an inflorescence
study_design: experimental floral/inflorescence manipulations with paternity and selfing
notes: Natural focal flowers are adichogamous. Experimental segregation of sex roles among flowers reduces geitonogamy and can increase outcross siring; this establishes conflict and alternative function but does not relabel the natural architecture as already segregated.

study_design: floral positional and evolutionary analysis
notes: Primary paper explicitly treats segregation of pollen and stigmas, but the present source screen does not promote the hypothesized interference mechanism to a direct experimental conflict receipt.

study_design: reproductive-biology field study

study_design: controlled self/cross pollination and ovule-development histology
notes: Self-pollination yields lower seed set and self-sterility is mechanistically resolved, but this does not by itself identify male-female interference as the selective conflict maintaining the floral polymorphism.

study_design: controlled self-before-compatible pollen timing experiment across three style morphs
notes: Prior self pollen reduces outcrossed seed set in morph- and timing-dependent fashion; tristyly is retained as a polymorphic architecture rather than forced into a binary structural outcome.

study_design: greenhouse self/cross and pollen-chase experiments
notes: Previously or simultaneously applied self pollen reduced seed set in two of three chase tests; the primary source does not establish a differentiated architecture resolving that cost.

study_design: controlled compatible/incompatible pollen dosage and timing experiment
notes: Most compatible/incompatible mixtures did not reduce seed set; clogging appeared only under an extreme long-styled treatment. Authors conclude pollen clogging was unlikely to play a major role in the evolution/maintenance of distyly.

study_design: histology plus mixed self/outcross pollination experiment
notes: Self pollen germinates and penetrates ovules; adding self pollen with outcross pollen reduces seed set by about 42%, supporting an ovule-usurpation cost without a directly established separated architecture in the cited source.

shared_structure: moving style-anther system within one-day hermaphroditic flowers
study_design: within-day floral-behaviour observations across flexistylous morphs
notes: Style movement clearly separates stigma receptivity from pollen presentation and promotes outcrossing. The cited primary source does not independently isolate male-female interference from anti-selfing/inbreeding-avoidance explanations, so conflict remains UNRESOLVED.
